name: 0/1 cusp, the starting view
note: The lab's own starting group, μ = 2i. Two wall spheres and pearls that just touch, spread in every direction by the third map.

name: 0/1 cusp, one row of pearls
note: The same group without the third map, seen from above. The pearls and the round gaps between them together make the Apollonian gasket.

name: 1/15 cusp, spirals
note: A classic cusp. The strings of pearls wind into spirals before they close up. Two maps, seen from above.

name: 1/2 cusp
note: μ = 1 + √3·i. Two maps. The picture is mirror-symmetric, with round windows between the strings of pearls.

name: 1/3 cusp
note: Turned out through the middle of a round gap, which gives the picture a half-turn symmetry. Third map on.

name: 2/5 cusp
note: Two maps. A short chain of pearls runs between two large ones, and the picture has a half-turn symmetry.

name: 1/5 cusp
note: Third map on. Two large pearls joined by a short chain, with round windows on either side.

name: 1/4 cusp
note: Two maps, seen from above. One wall sphere, with strings of pearls closing around round windows.

name: 5/13 cusp, branching
note: 5/13 is a ratio of Fibonacci numbers, like 1/2, 1/3, 2/5 and 3/8 before it. The pearls thin out into branches.

name: 8/21 cusp, near the golden mean
note: The next fraction in the same sequence: 8/21 is close to 0.382, one minus the golden mean. Fine branches of pearls stand around one wall sphere.

name: Above the 3/10 cusp
note: μ raised by 0.09 from the 3/10 cusp into the family. The strings of pearls have come apart into one loose chain.

name: Above the 1/2 cusp
note: μ raised by 0.17 from the 1/2 cusp. The strings of pearls no longer close up.

name: Inside, near the 0/1 cusp
note: μ = 0.1 + 1.95i, a little above the boundary. Two wall spheres with horns that curl but do not close.

name: 1/3 cusp, leaning in depth
note: The two maps of the 1/3 cusp turned 25° about the x-axis, which gives μ a j part. The walls now cut the group at a slant, so the pearls come out in unequal sizes.

name: 2/5 cusp, leaning in depth
note: The 2/5 cusp turned 20° about the x-axis, with the third map on.

name: 0/1 cusp, leaning 30°
note: μ = √3·i + j: the starting group turned 30° about the x-axis. Two maps, seen from above.

name: Leaning 30°, seen across
note: The same leaning group with the third map on, seen from the side: a disc of pearls with round windows.

name: Leaning both ways
note: μ = 0.5 + 1.7i + 0.5j: a real part and a j part at once, a little inside the boundary.

name: Stretched in depth
note: μ = 2i with the third map's step doubled (L = 2), so the rows of pearls stand twice as far apart in depth.

name: 0/1 cusp, sphere moved to one side
note: The starting group with two maps. The sphere sits to one side of the big gap, so the pearls close into a ring around one large window.

name: 0/1 cusp, sphere close to a wall
note: Two maps. The sphere sits low in the gap, close to one wall. That wall becomes a large ball inside a collar of pearls.

name: 0/1 cusp, third map: moved back
note: The starting group, turned out from a point one unit further back. The two wall spheres are joined by a net of pearls with large round windows.

name: 0/1 cusp, third map: across and back
note: The same group again, with the sphere one unit to the side and one unit back. The windows now face the camera.

name: 0/1 cusp, third map: close to a wall
note: The sphere sits half way between the middle of the gap and one wall, so one wall sphere grows and the other shrinks.

name: 1/2 cusp, gap under the upper wall
note: Two maps. From this gap the picture is a disc of pearls with two round windows.

name: 1/2 cusp, small sphere, narrow gap
note: A small sphere in a narrow gap beside the lower wall. The wall fills the middle and the pearls nearest the sphere stand in a ring around it.

name: 1/3 cusp, through a side gap
note: Two maps. The sphere has left the middle gap for the one beside it, so the half-turn symmetry is gone and the disc opens on one side.

name: 1/3 cusp, beside the large pearls
note: A small sphere in a narrow gap. The pearls next to it come out large and the rest of the disc is cut by three round bays.

name: 1/4 cusp, between the strings
note: Two maps. A small sphere between two strings of pearls: the nearest pearl comes out large and the strings fan out behind it.

name: 1/4 cusp, sphere lifted off the plane
note: The sphere of the 1/4 cusp entry raised half a unit out of the plane the pearls lie in. The flat disc curls into a bowl under one wall sphere.

name: 2/5 cusp, sphere in the middle gap
note: Two maps. The sphere sits in the gap between the two large pearls, which come out at opposite ends of the picture.

name: 1/15 cusp, through the opposite gap
note: The spirals from the gap on the other side of the strip: one wall sphere with the spirals wound around it.

name: Leaning 30°, lifted off the plane
note: μ = √3·i + j with two maps. The sphere is raised half a unit in depth, so the two wall spheres lean together inside a ring of pearls.

name: Leaning 30°, third map: moved back
note: The leaning group with the third map on, turned out from a narrow gap one unit back. One pearl comes out large in front of a disc with round windows.
